# Error Handling Checklist: SPEC-013A1 - GitHub Sync Automation and Poller Lifecycle

**Purpose**: Validate error-handling requirement quality for GitHub API failures, transport errors, bounded retry/backoff, partial pages, stale leases, disabled scopes, overlap rejection, manual retry, cursor preservation, and sanitized observability.
**Created**: 2026-05-23
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec require observable lifecycle state for failed, partial, stale-recovered, skipped-disabled, skipped-overlap, and rejected-overlap outcomes? [Completeness, Spec FR-012, Spec FR-013, Spec FR-023, Spec FR-029]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec require failed automatic sync attempts to preserve the prior last success cursor and expose failure time, failure counter, last error, next retry time, and next retry reason? [Completeness, Spec User Story 3, Spec FR-014, Spec FR-018]
- [x] CHK003 Are GitHub boundary failure categories complete enough to distinguish transport timeout/network failures, rate limits, auth/scope failures, 4xx/5xx responses, malformed JSON, unexpected page shape, invalid issue schema, database errors, and unknown failures? [Completeness, Spec FR-041, Plan §Observability Design, Data Model §Sync Run]
- [x] CHK004 Are malformed or partial GitHub issue page requirements explicit about page-atomic validation, cursor effect, and whether the run is `failed` or `partial` when a later page fails after earlier pages were fetched? [Coverage, Spec FR-042, Data Model §Partial Run State, Contract §GET /api/github/sync]
- [x] CHK005 Are stale lease requirements complete enough to record stale recovery before a replacement run proceeds without operator data repair? [Completeness, Spec FR-019, Spec SC-006, Data Model §Poller Lifecycle Control]
- [x] CHK006 Are disabled scope requirements complete enough to prevent future automatic ticks while preserving manual sync fallback and readable historical run evidence? [Completeness, Spec FR-021, Spec FR-027, Spec FR-035]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is retry/backoff precedence defined clearly for valid `Retry-After`, valid future `X-RateLimit-Reset`, invalid or past retry headers, exponential backoff fallback, workspace caps, and API-visible cap/fallback diagnostics? [Clarity, Spec FR-043, Data Model §Poller Lifecycle Control, Contract §GET /api/github/sync]
- [x] CHK008 Are manual retry requirements clear that manual sync may bypass automatic backoff only after acquiring the same overlap lease and without corrupting the success cursor? [Clarity, Spec Assumptions, Contract §POST /api/github/sync]
- [x] CHK009 Are overlap errors clear enough for same-scope manual requests to return deterministic 409 details with active run details and retry guidance? [Clarity, Spec FR-007, Spec FR-026, Contract §POST /api/github/sync]
- [x] CHK010 Are sanitized diagnostics requirements clear enough to prevent raw GitHub response bodies, authorization headers, tokens, credentials, API keys, and matched secret substrings from reaching API JSON, activity payloads, run details, or health summaries? [Security, Spec FR-039, Plan §Observability Design, Contract §GET /api/github/sync]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are lifecycle cursor rules consistent across failed, partial, skipped, stale-recovered, disabled, and manual fallback outcomes? [Consistency, Spec FR-014, Spec FR-015, Data Model §Sync Cursor]
- [x] CHK012 Are GitHub Sync API/UI observability requirements consistent with the decision to avoid a new telemetry service or generic scheduler settings surface? [Consistency, Spec FR-030, Spec FR-040, Plan §Out Of Scope]
- [x] CHK013 Are disabled controls and feature-flag-off states consistently defined as no automatic polling, without changing the existing manual sync compatibility baseline? [Consistency, Spec FR-006, Spec FR-021, Spec FR-027, Spec SC-007]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK014 Can reviewers objectively verify failure category, cursor preservation, backoff state, next retry reason/time, and sanitized failure text through documented lifecycle API/UI evidence? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec SC-002, Spec FR-023, Contract §GET /api/github/sync]
- [x] CHK015 Can reviewers objectively verify partial bounded stops and malformed-page outcomes without relying on hidden logs or process memory? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec SC-003, Data Model §Partial Run State]
- [x] CHK016 Can reviewers objectively verify manual retry after automatic failure/backoff/disablement without cursor corruption? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec SC-001, Spec SC-007, Contract §POST /api/github/sync]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are rate-limit and secondary-rate-limit cases represented as bounded retry states rather than unbounded scheduler loops? [Coverage, Spec FR-018, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK018 Are transport and GitHub API failures required to be observable even when no compatibility `github_syncs` row can safely represent lifecycle detail? [Coverage, Plan §Data Model, Data Model §Sync Run]
- [x] CHK019 Are rollback or emergency disablement paths specified to preserve data readability, manual sync, and future stale recovery for already-owned runs? [Coverage, Spec FR-021, Spec FR-027, Spec FR-035]

## Notes

- Initial error-handling checklist found three gaps around stable GitHub boundary failure taxonomy, malformed or partial page semantics, and retry signal precedence/cap visibility.
- Remediation added Spec FR-041 through FR-043, Plan Observability Design and Verification Plan bullets, Data Model failure category/backoff/malformed-page rules, and Contract diagnostics/backoff/malformed-page response rules.
